items.title: "Muse Gadgets" turns AI hardware into an open-source DIY project
items.summary: Meta announced Muse Gadgets, an open-source project that lets hobbyists build their own AI hardware using ESP32 boards and connect it to Meta's AI agent Muse. The team also produced 5,000 units of the "Muse Home Link," a USB-C device for smart home control. The open-source approach also helps Meta figure out which AI hardware form factors people actually want. The article "Muse Gadgets" turns AI hardware into an open-source DIY project appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: Another OpenAI safety departure adds to a pattern of researchers leaving with public warnings
items.summary: David Robinson, who worked on safety systems at OpenAI, left the company and is blasting its safety culture. He points to AI agents that were accidentally released and a model that bypassed its internet access restrictions. AI companies need to operate like nuclear power plants, with multiple layers of redundancy instead of trial and error. The article Another OpenAI safety departure adds to a pattern of researchers leaving with public warnings appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: Deepmind researchers propose "Artificial Symbiotic Intelligence" as an alternative to the singularity
items.summary: According to researchers at the Deepmind Institute, general AI won't emerge as a single supermodel but as a network of cooperating agents and humans. What will matter most, they argue, is not model size but the rules and institutions that govern how they all work together. The article Deepmind researchers propose "Artificial Symbiotic Intelligence" as an alternative to the singularity appeared first on The Decoder .
items.summary_zh: 根據深度思維研究院（Deepmind Institute）研究人員的說法，通用人工智慧不會以單一超級模型的形式出現，而是作為一個由協同運作的代理程式和人類組成的網路。他們主張，最重要的不是模型大小，而是管理牠們如何共同運作的規則與機制。這篇題為「Deepmind 研究人員提出『人工共生智慧』作為奇異點的替代方案」的文章最初發表於 The Decoder。

items.title: AI agents build 3D scenes from photos but have no idea if they got it right
items.summary: A new approach called LEGO-Anything turns single photos into editable Blender code for 3D scenes. GPT-6 Astra leads the accompanying benchmark with up to 53 percent reconstruction accuracy. The biggest weakness across all tested agents is that they can't judge their own geometric accuracy any better than a coin flip. The article AI agents build 3D scenes from photos but have no idea if they got it right appeared first on The Decoder .
items.summary_zh: 一項名為 LEGO-Anything 的新方法能將單張照片轉化為可用於 3D 場景的可編輯 Blender 程式碼。GPT-6 Astra 在隨附的基準測試中領先，重建準確度高達 53%。所有受測代理程式最大的弱點在於，牠們判斷自身幾何準確度的能力並不比擲硬幣好多少。這篇題為「AI agents build 3D scenes from photos but have no idea if they got it right」的文章首先發表於 The Decoder。
